chunks: We mentioned to him al-Kufa and what land tax had been imposed upon it, and what the members of his household had done there. So he said: 'Whoever accepted Islam voluntarily, his land was left in his possession, and one-tenth (ushr) was taken from him from what the sky and rivers watered, and half the tenth (5%) from what was irrigated by rope/bucket — this applies to what they cultivated from it. As for what they did not cultivate, the Imam takes it and leases it to those who cultivate it; and it belonged to the Muslims, and upon the lessees in their shares was the tenth and half the tenth. And there is no zakat on less than five awsuq.

As for what was taken by the sword, that is up to the Imam — he leases it as he sees fit, just as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did at Khaybar: he contracted its black (cultivated land) and its white (palm trees), meaning its land and its palms. The people say it is not valid to contract out land and palm trees, yet the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) contracted Khaybar; and upon the contractors, besides the land contract, was the tenth and half the tenth in their shares.

He also said: The people of al-Taif accepted Islam, and the tenth and half the tenth were imposed upon them. The people of Mecca — the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) entered it by force; they were captives in his hand, and he freed them and said: Go, for you are all free (tulaqa).

key_terms.الأوساق: Awsuq — plural of wasq, a grain measure (approx. 60 sa', ~130 kg); minimum threshold for zakat
key_terms.الخراج: Kharaj — land tax imposed on non-Muslims or conquered territories
key_terms.الطلقاء: Tulaqa — 'the freed ones', the name given to Meccans liberated at the Conquest of Mecca
key_terms.العشر: Ushr — one-tenth (10%) tithe on rain-fed or river-irrigated produce
key_terms.قبالة: Qabala — agricultural lease contract; 'qabbala' means to lease/contract land
key_terms.نصف العشر: Nisf al-ushr — half the tenth (5%), applied to artificially irrigated crops

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of zakat and land tax (kharaj) for agricultural produce according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: This hadith details Imam al-Ridha's (AS) legal rulings on land tax and zakat for agricultural produce. The Imam distinguishes between lands whose inhabitants converted voluntarily — where the ushr (10% or 5% depending on irrigation) applies — and lands conquered by force, which fall under the Imam's discretionary authority to lease. The Imam cites the Prophet's precedent at Khaybar and the distinct treatment of al-Taif (voluntary conversion with tithe) and Mecca (conquest followed by manumission). This teaching clarifies the Imam's sovereign role in managing conquered land for the Muslim community's benefit.
